input.quote: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice. Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection.
input.rationale: Section 4.4 is the only audit right binding us (no other inspection, verification or system-access right appears in the Agreement, including Exhibit B revenue sharing and payment terms). It already limits inspections to once each calendar year, requires an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to us, and puts costs on Commerce One, and it grants no access to our systems. It fails the fallback on two material terms: notice is merely "reasonable" rather than a fixed minimum of 15 days, and cost-shifting is triggered by an underpayment of only 5% rather than the fallback 10% threshold. We therefore target the fallback with two surgical numeric edits and do not pursue the preferred additions (business hours, confidentiality-bound auditor, off-site where possible), which we note in negotiation only.

mappings.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
mappings.quote: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year

mappings.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.

proposal.summary: Set a 15-day notice period and raise the audit cost-shifting threshold to 10% underpayment in Section 4.4.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have fixed the audit notice period at fifteen (15) days' prior notice rather than undefined "reasonable notice", and moved the cost-shifting trigger to underpayments exceeding ten percent, which is our fallback audit position. Annual frequency, the independent accountant and Commerce One bearing audit costs are unchanged.
